import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' to datetime format
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Create a new column for total sales per product
sales_per_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set the order of the products based on total sales
sales_per_product = sales_per_product.sort_values('total', ascending=False)

# Create a bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.barplot(data=sales_per_product, x='total', y='product', palette='viridis')

# Adding titles and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Product', fontsize=14)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd

# Create a bar plot

sns.barplot(data=sales_per_product, x='total', y='product', palette='viridis')
